attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his own view.

semantics.note: 'Strong intuition... will be under 20%' reads as a high-confidence forecast, not 'likely'. The drafter's modality weakens it, and the proposition drops the full-jobs consequence clause. 'Perhaps under 10%' is hedged and not scored.

contract.note: Fair plain reading: under 20% is the firm part, under 10% is tentative, Mythos Preview only, RLI automation rate. It treats the physical and jobs clauses sensibly. Undefined terms like 'meaningful' and 'small' leave the result open to interpretation.

evidence.note: Original RLI paper (Oct 2025) with a 2.5% top score. It predates Mythos, so it is baseline context only.

Anthropic's own July 2026 disclosure. Mythos Preview learned faster on one simulated locomotion task, but neither model completed the harder courses. This is an isolated task gain, not evidence about whole physical jobs.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no authenticated Mythos Preview RLI result, so the main numerical forecast can't be checked. The only robotics evidence is a company disclosure of a gain on one isolated task, which the contract says doesn't settle the physical-jobs clause. No deadline was given and no conclusive event happened, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion. The astronomical figure comes from someone else's joke, but Marcus endorses the claim it is used in.

semantics.note: Firm language ('absolutely sure', 'not going to') makes this a scored forecast. The threshold is kept, and no deadline was stated.

contract.note: Fair, ordinary reading. It is supported by a lasting break or ceiling below the threshold, contradicted by validated doublings that reach it, and saturation alone settles nothing.

evidence.note: METR's May 2026 report says its benchmark is saturated, with a time horizon above two work days. That is a measurement limit, not a capability break or a threshold crossing.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given. The evidence shows neither a validated crossing of the threshold nor an established lasting ceiling, and benchmark saturation is explicitly ruled out as deciding the claim, so it remains unresolved.
